previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, end-stage renal disease status post kidney transplant, and severe peripheral vascular disease was admitted for severe left leg pain due to necrotic infection and gangrene. He underwent a two-stage left below-knee amputation: first a guillotine amputation followed by re-amputation with closure. He received blood transfusions preoperatively to support hemoglobin levels and was treated with intravenous vancomycin, ciprofloxacin, and metronidazole for infection, later transitioning to oral antibiotics. Pain was managed with a Dilaudid PCA initially, then oral hydromorphone, acetaminophen, and pregabalin. The nephrology team optimized tacrolimus and blood pressure medications to protect his transplant. The wound healed well, and he was discharged to extended care with plans for rehabilitation and outpatient follow-up. His right hand showed dry gangrene of multiple digits, but no acute intervention was needed.
problems: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of extremities with gangrene, left leg
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic peripheral angiopathy with gangrene

diabetes mellitus, presenting with cold like symptoms, including 
rhinorrhea, one night of night sweats, and nausea today, such 
that he was unable to eat or take his medications. 

According to Mr. ___, he presented to the ED initially on ___ 
with wheezing and cough x1 day as well as back pain. He reports 
that the wheezing felt more like it was upper airway than in his 
lungs. He denies any shortness of breath, sputum, upper airway 
congestion, rhinorrhea, sore throat, or sick contacts. He was 
nauseas the day prior to presentation so he forgot to take his 
blood pressure medications. He denies diarrhea or new abdominal 
pain (reports some baseline abdominal pain for which he is being 
worked up for celiac disease). He otherwise denied chest pain, 
palpitations, leg edema. 

In the ED, initial vitals were 99.7 84 235/115 20 97% RA. This 
then improved to 168/71 with addition of home clonidine patch, 
labetalol, nifedipine and chlorthalidone. Exam was notable for 
normal neurologic exam and no focal or reproducible tenderness 
of the spine. Labs were notable for CBC near baseline, Chem with 
Cr 3.3 which is near baseline, negative influenza, UA not 
concerning for UTI. troponin was 0.14 and downtrended to 0.12. 
Transplant ultrasound showed an AV fistula at likely site of 
prior biopsy, and CXR showing no focal consolidation and mild 
interstitial opacities. Renal transplant was consulted and 
recommended continuing home regimen, with no specific reason for 
admission from renal standpoint as largely at baseline. 

He was given home meds including antihypertensives, 
immunosuppressants. He was noted to have a desaturation on 
continuous pulse ox while asleep. He says he has a known history 
of sleep apnea shown on prior sleep studies. Most recently he 
had a home sleep study in ___ and there was a plan for him 
to have an inpatient sleep study as well. He currently owns a 
CPAP machine but has not used this for years due to discomfort. 
An attempt was made to arrange for home O2 for him pending more 
sleep studies, which this required inpatient admission.  He 
reports he would sleep with nasal cannula. 

Upon arrival to the floor, the patient endorses the history 
above. He reports feeling improved though his cough still 
bothers him.

less apparent than on most recent prior, likely due to 
differences in technique, though there may be some residual mild 
interstitial edema although atypical pneumonia cannot be

___ US Transplant Kidney, Aorta and Branches
FINDINGS:  
- The left lower quadrant transplant renal morphology is normal. 
 Specifically, the cortex is of normal thickness and 
echogenicity, pyramids are normal, there is no urothelial 
thickening, and renal sinus fat is normal.  There is no 
hydronephrosis and no perinephric fluid collection.  Two simple 
renal cysts are identified.  At the lower pole of the kidney is 
a highly vascular structure visualized under color Doppler with 
markedly elevated peak systolic velocity of approximately 200 
cm/second.  Findings are suggestive of an underlying AV fistula. 

- The resistive index of intrarenal arteries ranges from 0.73 to 
0.77 previously 0.66-0.8.  The main renal artery shows a normal 
waveform, with prompt systolic upstroke and continuous antegrade 
diastolic flow, with peak systolic velocity of 85 cm/second.  
Vascularity is symmetric throughout transplant. The transplant 
renal vein is patent and shows normal waveform. 
IMPRESSION:  
- Findings suggestive of an AV fistula at the lower pole of the 
left lower 
quadrant transplant kidney. Resistive indices ranging from 
0.73-0.77, a similar range compared to prior.
